model_result.answer_summary: Q is Al; C·xH2O is AlF3·3H2O (C = AlF3, x = 3); D is Na3AlF6 (cryolite). The proposed formulas reproduce 39.16% water, 32.85% Na, and 12.85% Al at the printed precision and satisfy AlF3 + 3 NaF -> Na3AlF6.
assumptions: Atomic masses H = 1.008, O = 16.00, F = 19.00, Na = 22.99, and Al = 26.98 are taken exactly as printed on PDF source page 5.
A displayed percentage with two decimal places denotes the closed half-quantum interval around that value, so the quantum is 0.01 percentage point.
The ordinary-chemistry Hall-Heroult classification is represented explicitly: cryolite Na3AlF6 is the fluoride medium used in industrial aluminium production.

The pH-controlled precipitate C is interpreted as the sodium-free metal fluoride precursor, and the schematic C + NaF -> D is modeled as atom-conserving uptake of an integral number of NaF formula units with no additional product.
source_gaps: The problem text does not itself define cryolite or state its formula/industrial role; this allowed ordinary-chemistry fact is separated as IndustrialFluoridePair and grounded in USGS and PubChem references in answer.md.

The problem text does not explicitly say that C is sodium-free. Bare formula arithmetic also permits the formal countermodel Na2AlF5·6H2O, which has the same rounded water percentage and converts to Na3AlF6 with one NaF. The standard answer therefore depends on phase-identity chemistry at pH about 4; Lean exposes this condition rather than claiming unconditional numerical uniqueness.
